__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Application Prometheus
__inputs.description: Choose the Prometheus data source that scrapes the BFF /metrics listener and contains dial_chat_generations_active with otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api". An OTLP data source may use different metric names or labels.

title: DIAL BFF - Request latency and Core attribution
description: Whole-period endpoint latency and request-local Core attribution. Requests count when their transport ends. Core time is the union of observed Core activity; outside-Core time includes Chat processing and other waits. Default: last 24 hours, ordinary transports.

list.name: transport
list.label: Transport
list.description: Ordinary excludes the explicitly classified long-lived streaming routes. It still includes synchronous generation and file transfers. All combines both classes.

list.name: trace_service
list.label: Trace service.name
list.description: Actual OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, independent of metric scope. Literal service name; quotes/backslashes require custom Explore JSON escaping.

list.name: trace_min_duration
list.label: Trace minimum duration
list.description: Only affects the optional Tempo table. Independent of metric thresholds, workload, endpoint, transport and outcome filters.

options.content: **Compare endpoints over the full selected period (default: last 24 hours).** Requests count when they end; open streams appear later. **Core** is observed time with at least one Core operation active, including network/transfer. **Outside Core** includes Chat processing, other dependencies and delivery waits; it is not CPU time. Ordinary transports are selected by default. Missing data stays missing; new measurements have no historical backfill.

panels.title: Ended requests in period (estimated)
panels.description: One total-phase observation per ended matched request. All selected outcomes count; open requests are absent. Increase is a scrape-based estimate, not an audit count.

panels.title: Mean request duration in period
panels.description: Weighted duration across ended requests in the full selected period. Includes all selected outcomes and statuses; change the filters to compare a specific population.

panels.title: Core share of request time in period
panels.description: Core-active time divided by total request time across the same ended requests. Concurrent Core calls overlap once within each request. This is a ratio of sums, not an average of per-request percentages.

targets.legendFormat: Core share of request time in period

panels.title: All endpoints — latency in period
panels.description: Each row is one method and matched route template over the whole period, including endpoints outside the top ten. Sort by count, mean or percentile. Percentiles are histogram estimates and are omitted when above the last finite 3600-second bucket; consult the slow-request table. Low counts make tail estimates less representative.

panels.title: Top 10 endpoints — mean duration in period
panels.description: Ranks endpoints by mean duration over the full selected period. Low-volume endpoints can rank highly; compare their request counts in the table.

panels.title: Top 10 endpoints — accumulated request time
panels.description: Total duration of ended requests over the selected period. Concurrent requests contribute independently, so the sum can exceed wall-clock time; it is neither CPU usage nor time spent inside Core.

panels.title: All endpoints — Core and outside-Core attribution
panels.description: Components are recorded for the same request population at transport settlement. Core is the union of observed request-local Core intervals, clipped at settlement. Outside Core is total minus that union and includes Chat work, IdP/other dependencies, scheduling and client delivery waits. Core includes network/transfer and may overlap local work; it is not Core server CPU time. Requests without Core calls have an observed zero Core component.

panels.title: Top 10 slowest endpoints — mean time components
panels.description: Same whole-period mean ranking as above. Each horizontal bar adds mean Core-active time and mean outside-Core time to the mean total duration. Concurrent Core calls count once. The attribution table includes every endpoint and can be sorted by outside-Core time.

panels.title: All endpoints — requests above duration thresholds
panels.description: Estimated ended requests strictly above each boundary in the full period. Counts are rounded for display only. The 1-hour share explains missing tail quantiles: p95 is omitted when more than 5% exceed 1 hour, and p99 when more than 1% do. No requests or missing telemetry gives no percentage.

options.content:
Select a **Trace datasource (Tempo)**, set **Trace service.name** to the deployed `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (default `@epam/chat-api`), and choose **Trace minimum duration**. The table uses this service, threshold and the dashboard time range. **Metric workload, endpoint, transport and outcome filters do not apply to this table.** Select a Tempo source scoped to the intended environment or add verified resource filters in the query.

Open a **Trace / span** link to inspect one request. Timing columns are seconds and carry the same Core/outside-Core interpretation as the metrics. Results include up to 100 matching traces and 20 spans per spanset, sorted by total duration among those returned. Sampling, retention and search limits apply: this is not an exhaustive daily ranking of every request. The collapsed section does not load its panels until expanded.

panels.title: Slow request instances — longest among returned matches
panels.description: Independent Tempo search over the dashboard time range. Only the trace service and minimum-duration variables apply. At most 100 traces, with up to 20 spans per spanset; sorting returned matches does not establish the globally slowest requests. Click Trace / span to open the trace at the matching timing span.

targets.query: { resource.service.name = ${trace_service:json} && span.dial.chat.http.request.timing = true && span:duration > $trace_min_duration } | select(span.http.route, span.http.request.method, span.dial.chat.http.duration.total, span.dial.chat.http.duration.core, span.dial.chat.http.duration.chat)
